guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2.0 authorization code flows for user-owned applications, and the connected person's OAuth token acts on their behalf. The least documented scope covering the confirmed issue read is read_api, which is broad read access to the API, so the app's read-only behavior must be enforced in code.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read issue titles in projects the connected person can access, with pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Register a user-owned OAuth application before authorization
findings.detail: Authorization code flows require the application to be registered first in the user's account Applications page, which provides an Application ID and Client Secret, and a redirect URI must be configured.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to every customer connection using user OAuth.

evidence.quote: Authorization code (with or without PKCE) flow requires application to be
registered first via the /user_settings/applications page in your user’s account.

findings.title: Use the authorization code flow with PKCE or code flow and refresh tokens
findings.detail: The authorize endpoint takes the requested scope parameter, the token endpoint exchanges the code, and access tokens expire after two hours by default; integrations must use the refresh_token to obtain new tokens.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to each customer's connected account after authorization.

findings.title: read_api grants read access to the API including projects
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, which covers listing issues the connected person can access; the grant does not limit access to issues, so it is broader than the request and the app must not call write endpoints.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the issue title read action for the connected person.

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.
Scope Access read_api Grants read access to the API. Sufficient for queries.
List all issues Lists all issues the authenticated user has access to. By default, returns only issues created by the current user.

findings.title: Paginate issue lists with the Link header
findings.detail: Responses are paginated with a default of 20 items and a maximum of 100 per page; the Link header provides next, prev, first and last links, and the app should follow only the given next link rather than building its own URL.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when reading issue titles across multiple pages.

steps.title: Register a user-owned GitLab OAuth application
steps.detail: Register a user-owned OAuth application in the GitLab account Applications page (Access > Applications), enter the name and redirect URI, select read_api, and copy the Application ID and Client Secret. Use the authorization code flow with PKCE as the single chosen client type; the client must not include the secret in the token exchange when PKCE is used.
steps.doneWhen: The application shows an Application ID and secret, and the redirect URI matches the callback the app will use.

steps.title: Start consent and verify the callback state
steps.detail: Redirect the customer to the GitLab authorize endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, state, scope=read_api, code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256. The customer approves in the browser; the app verifies the returned state matches before continuing.
steps.doneWhen: The callback contains a code and the same state value that was sent.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for tokens
steps.detail: POST the returned code and the PKCE code_verifier to the token endpoint with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id and redirect_uri. Do not send client_secret when using PKCE. The response includes access_token, refresh_token and expires_in (7200 by default).
steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token, token_type bearer, refresh_token and expires_in.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles in one accessible project
steps.detail: Call the documented List all project issues endpoint as the connected person with the OAuth bearer token, for one project the person can access. The default unfiltered /issues endpoint returns only issues created by the current user, so the project-scoped endpoint is used instead. Read the title string from each element of the returned array. Use per_page=100, the documented maximum. Only GET is used.
steps.doneWhen: The response is a JSON array and each element exposes a title string. Continue to the next step if a Link header with rel=next is present. Boundary check: confirm the token is OAuth with read_api, and confirm the outgoing request log contains only this GET request and no create, update or delete calls.

steps.title: Follow the Link header to read the next page
steps.detail: Read the rel="next" URL from the Link header of the first response and request it unchanged with the same bearer token. Continue until the Link header has no rel="next" entry or the array is empty.
steps.doneWhen: The next response is a JSON array of issue titles and the stopping condition is documented: the Link header is absent or the array is empty.

steps.title: Continue issue title pagination until the documented end
steps.detail: Repeat the request using only the URL from the rel=next entry in the Link header of the previous response, without building or changing the URL. Read title from each array element on every page. Stop when the Link header is absent and the array is empty, which is the documented end of the collection. Two pages alone are not a complete listing. Only GET is used.
